title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples & Docs Ops Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates the standards, templates, and operating procedures that the Developer Experience (DevEx) team uses to produce SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and docs-site operations. The goal is to keep onboarding friction low, maintain consistent quality across SDKs, and ensure fast, reliable documentation updates tied to releases and support tickets.

Scope: Applies to all public SDKs (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Java), quickstart samples, API examples published on docs.redwood.ai, and the docs-site publishing workflow. Excludes internal RFCs and personal notes.

Owners and Roles

- Document owner: DevEx Content Team (primary contact: Sofia Patel)
- Technical owner: SDK/Platform Engineering (for code accuracy)
- QA owner: Docs QA (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-qa-process)
- Support liaison: Developer Support (triage and canonical fixes)

Standards and Writing Guidelines

- Audience: software engineers and ML engineers integrating inference into applications. Write for engineers who need copy-paste examples that work end-to-end.
- Tone: concise, active voice, preference for example-first (short working sample before deep explanation).
- Formatting: use short intro, bullets for steps, numbered procedures for commands, and an FAQ section for common pitfalls. Include one runnable example per language.
- API surface: always include authentication snippet, basic request, streaming (if available), and error handling.

SDK Guide Template (required fields)

1. Title and short description (1 sentence).
2. Prerequisites (account, API key, recommended model and region).
3. Install + quick import (single command).
4. Minimal working example (10-20 lines, copy-paste runnable).
5. Common options and patterns (timeouts, batching, retries).
6. Streaming example (if SDK supports it).
7. Migration notes (if breaking changes).
8. Testing and local sandboxing tips.
9. Troubleshooting + links to canonical support articles.
10. API reference link and link to SDK repo.

Checklist before publishing SDK guide

- [ ] Code runs in CI sample runner (integration tests).
- [ ] Linting and formatting applied (prettier/black/gofmt).
- [ ] Security review for secrets handling.
- [ ] Code examples pinned to specific SDK version.
- [ ] Reviewed by SDK owner and one reviewer from Platform.
- [ ] Metadata tags and labels added for search.

Quickstarts & Templates

Purpose: Provide minimal apps that demonstrate a complete integration: authentication, request, output handling, and basic error handling. Quickstarts should be runnable in <5 minutes.

Canonical quickstart templates (location: /repos/docs-quickstarts):
- simple-generate-python: Fastest path to text generation with Redwood API.
- node-chat-app-template: WebSocket chat client + server-side token handling.
- embeddings-search-go: Build a vector search prototype using Redwood embeddings.
- ops-and-monitoring-example: Example showing how to emit tracing and cost telemetry.

Template checklist:

- README with prerequisites and one-line run command.
- Dockerfile + optional local-compose for local testing.
- CI job that runs smoke test and lints examples.
- .env.example (no secret values) and instructions for secrets management.

API Examples (best practices)

- Always show both REST/HTTP and SDK examples.
- Keep examples focused: do not demonstrate advanced features in the minimal example. Advanced features belong in a dedicated section below the minimal example.

Minimal HTTP example (curl):

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'

Minimal Python example (redwood-sdk):

from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-large", input="Summarize: The quarterly results...")
print(resp.output[0].content)

Docs Site Operating Procedures

Purpose: Ensure docs updates are reliable, quick to roll back, and linked to code releases.

Release workflow (for content changes tied to a release):
1. Create a docs branch: docs/<release>-<ticket-id>.
2. Add/update SDK guide and quickstart. Update metadata frontmatter (version, sdk_version).
3. Open PR against docs main branch. Assign to DevEx owner and SDK owner.
4. Docs CI runs: link check, sample-runner, lint, spellcheck.
5. After approval, merge to main. Merges to main trigger staging build.
6. Staging review: internal reviewers validate code samples.
7. Schedule publish: publish window aligned with release (default: 09:00 UTC next business day).
8. Post-publish smoke tests run against the live site.

Hotfix workflow (customer-impacting docs bug):

- Tag issue with priority P1/P2 and create hotfix branch docs/hotfix-<id>.
- Skip extended approvals: one reviewer + owner approval required.
- Merge to main and trigger immediate publish.

Docs QA checklist (pre-merge):

- [ ] All code blocks pass sample-runner.
- [ ] Images have alt text and are optimized.
- [ ] Links validated (no 4xx).
- [ ] Frontmatter includes version and labels.
- [ ] Author and reviewer metadata present.

Content lifecycle and deprecation policy

- Every public SDK guide must be reviewed annually. Maintainers will receive automated reminders 60/30/7 days before review due date.
- Deprecation: mark guides as deprecated at least 30 days before removal and provide migration steps.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (FAQ + canonical KB mapping)

1) Authentication errors: "401 / invalid_api_key"
- Symptom: curl/SDK returns 401.
- Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY exported in shell or passed in client constructor. For rotating keys, confirm header name is Authorization: Bearer <KEY>. Link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/authentication-401.

2) Rate limit exceeded: "429" or "rate_limit"
- Symptom: Intermittent 429s under burst traffic.
- Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter and retry on idempotent calls. For high-throughput batch workloads, use dedicated capacity or configure bursting. Add sample code for backoff in SDK guides.

3) Streaming connection drops (WebSocket/HTTP2)
- Symptom: Partial response with connection reset.
- Canonical fix: Implement client re-connect logic with resume semantics where supported. Check network middleboxes (proxies) dropping long-lived connections. Provide sample keepalive and reconnect policy in node-chat-app-template.

4) Mismatched tokenization / unexpected truncation
- Symptom: Outputs truncated or unexpected behavior for long contexts.
- Canonical fix: Confirm model max_tokens and ensure client sends content_length hints where supported. Add guidance in SDK guide on handling long inputs (chunking + KV cache usage).

5) Embeddings mismatch across SDKs
- Symptom: Different embedding vectors between Python and Node SDKs for the same input.
- Canonical fix: Ensure both SDKs pin the same model version and that text-normalization (NFKC/NFD) steps are identical. Document normalization utility in SDK repos and include a one-line canonical normalizer.

Telemetry, Metrics, and KPIs for Docs

- Sample-runner pass rate (target >= 99% per merge).
- Time-to-publish for PR (median <= 24 hours for non-blocking changes).
- Top support articles coverage: aim to reduce repeat bug reports for top-10 issues by 50% q/q.

Housekeeping and Automation

- Sample-runner: CI job that executes all minimal examples in a sandbox environment; failures create Jira tickets auto-labelled docs-sample-failure.
- Auto-reminders: calendar invites for annual reviews.
- Issue templating: use dedicated docs issue template that captures reproducible steps, SDK version, region, and logs.

Related resources

- SDK repos: https://git.redwood.ai/org/sdk-templates
- Docs site repo & CI: https://git.redwood.ai/org/docs-site
- Support KB index: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds

Appendix: Example Labeling and Frontmatter

Frontmatter example (YAML at top of MD file):

---
title: "Python Quickstart: Text Generation"
version: "2025.04"
language: "python"
labels: ["quickstart","sdk","example","python"]
---

Contact and escalation

- First line: DevEx Content Team (devex@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: Pager for SDK owner (see team roster).
